subject: Brightline: post-call technical ops plan and next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Liam Baker <liam.baker@brightline.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Brightline — post-call technical recap and asks

Liam — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so the team and I are aligned, plus explicit asks so we can prep a focused technical deep-dive: 

Summary of what you shared (pain & goals)
- Primary pain: unpredictable P95 latency spikes during dayparts (current p95 ~700–900ms for interactive chat).
- Throughput profile: peak concurrent interactive sessions ~80, sustained token throughput ~4.5M tokens/day, batch/rerank workloads ~150 requests/min at night.
- Model constraints: prefer an open LLaMA-family model variant with ≥2048 context window; evaluation set includes long-form clinical summaries and short prompts for triage.
- Data/security: must run within a customer VPC (private control plane), KMS integration required, SOC2 + HITRUST checklist in procurement.

Redwood hypothesis and recommended initial SLOs (for discussion)
- Latency SLO: P50 <150ms, P95 <=300ms for 512-token requests (we'll need to confirm your typical token lengths).
- Throughput SLO: sustain 5M tokens/day with headroom for 2x burst capacity during peak.
- Availability: 99.95% for inference endpoints, with fallbacks to a lower-cost variant during capacity events.

Initial topology sketch (what we'll propose for the deep-dive)
- Private deployment in Brightline VPC across two AZs: 2 dedicated GPU pools (primary + warm standby) with autoscale thresholds by queue latency.
- Continuous batching + KV cache (prefix cache) to reduce per-token cost for repeated dialogs.
- Quantization candidate path: int8 or trimmed fp16 depending on model fidelity tests.
- Observability: token-level tracing + per-request debug mode for sampled requests.

Immediate asks / artifacts we need from you before the technical deep-dive:
1) Representative prompt set (we discussed short and long examples) — please attach as plain text.
2) A week of anonymized production traces (timestamps, token counts, request latencies) or a CSV export — low-sensitivity fields only.
3) Procurement contacts for SOC2/HIPAA mapping (you mentioned Sarah — cc'd to introduce if OK).

Next steps
- Proposed technical deep-dive: 60–75 minutes focused on topology, SLO tradeoffs, and a rough capacity/cost estimate. Can we target Tue Aug 24 or Wed Aug 25 (my team is in PDT)?
- I'll circulate a short agenda and our initial topology diagram + latency model before the call.

Attachments: call-notes-20270821.txt (raw notes), prompt_samples.txt (please review and augment).

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Liam Baker <liam.baker@brightline.health>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Mitchell <sarah.mitchell@brightline.health>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Brightline — post-call technical recap and asks

Thanks Soojin — this is a great concise summary. A few clarifications and items we attached: 

Clarifications
- Typical interactive session length: median 45 tokens, heavy tails up to ~1,200 tokens for discharge summaries. Our SLO focus should be on the 128–512 token range for triage UX and a separate band for long-form generation.
- Burst behavior: we see two regular bursts (08:00–10:30 ET and 20:00–22:30 ET) where concurrent requests jump ~2.5x.

Attached: prompt_samples.txt (expanded), latency_profile.csv (week of anonymized traces).

Procurement / security
- Sarah is our security/compliance lead and will own the SOC2/HIPAA checklist. Sarah, can we set an intro sync for next week?

A couple of questions for your team ahead of the deep-dive:
1) How much P95 improvement do you typically see from prefix caching for repeated-dialog flows?
2) For an open LLaMA-variant at ~7B, what ballpark GPU pool size should we expect for the target throughput?

Happy to go with Tue Aug 24 at 11:00 PT if that still works.

— Liam
Brightline Health
liam.baker@brightline.health | +1 617-555-0199
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Brightline — post-call technical recap and asks (internal)

Ben/Aditya — forwarding Brightline’s materials (prompt_samples.txt, latency_profile.csv) they sent this morning. High-level asks from Liam we should prepare for the deep-dive on Tue: 

1) Ballpark capacity for 7B LLaMA-like model to hit 5M tokens/day with p95 <=300ms (512 token band), handling 2.5x bursts to ~200 concurrent interactive sessions.
2) Expected P95 delta from enabling prefix/KV cache for repeated dialogs — can we provide a conservative estimate (e.g., 20–40% p95 reduction) and one optimistic number with a cache hit-rate assumption?
3) Quantization paths: quick note on int8 impact on latency and memory for a 7B candidate (keep fidelity caveats).
4) Preliminary cost delta: hosted vs dedicated vs private-reserved estimates (prefer per-token and per-hour GPU pool cost).

Please use the latency_profile.csv and prompt_samples.txt to run a small simulation (simple queueing + per-token service time) — we don't need full perf runs before the call, but deliverables for Tue's deep-dive: 
- Slide with topology sketch and autoscale thresholds
- one-page capacity/cost table (GPU types, node count estimate, expected p95)
- quick notes on security prerequisites for Private/VPC (KMS, network egress rules, logging hooks)

Attachments copied to this thread: latency_profile.csv, prompt_samples.txt. Also adding call-notes-20270821.txt for context.

Can one of you pick up the topology slide? Ben — I think you're best placed to do the autoscale thresholds. Aditya — can you run the simple token-level sim and give a GPU node estimate by EOD Mon?

Thanks — Soojin

--

I'll also include an estimate for using int8 quantization vs fp16 for the 7B candidate — likely 25–35% lower memory footprint and ~10–20% latency improvement (conservative).
